## What's new in 1.1.0

- **Video calls on Android and Windows.** During a call, press **Camera on** to send your camera. It never turns on by itself: every call starts with the camera off, and it turns off when the call ends.
  - **Android:** starts with the front camera. The switch button flips between the **front and back camera**. The first time, Android asks for camera permission.
  - **Windows:** the camera menu lists the **built-in webcam and any USB webcam**, so you can choose one. If the camera is blocked, turn on *Settings → Privacy & security → Camera → Let desktop apps access your camera*.
  - While a camera is on, the video fills the screen, with your own picture as a small self-view. The tile of whoever is speaking lights up green.
  - The Linux and Raspberry Pi desktop apps show incoming video (they can't send it yet). The headless node ignores video.
  - With *Everyone*, video works like the audio: the caller sees every member, and members see the caller.
  - Video is about 640×480 at up to 15 pictures per second. On weak Wi-Fi, pictures are skipped so the audio never lags.
  - On Android the camera pauses while the app is in the background (Android doesn't allow the camera there).

Upgrading: install over 1.0.x (same variant on Android). Settings and saved peers are kept. 1.1.0 and 1.0.x still talk to each other; video needs 1.1.0 on both ends.
